record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: Is a positive cosmological constant or dark-energy density around ΩΛ ≈ 0.7 genuinely established by observations, or could the inference be shaped by prior model expectations, supernova dimming from intergalactic dust, metallicity dependence, host-galaxy extinction, alternative cosmological fits, and the enormous mismatch between observed Λ and quantum-field-theory vacuum-energy predictions?

evidence.quote: A genial prediction or a prejudice which conditions the actual measures? Another open question.

Type Ia Supernovae have also possibly a metallicity dependence and this would imply that the evidence for a non-zero cosmological constant from the SNIa Hubble Diagram may be subject to corrections for metallicity which are as big as the effects of cosmology[238].

Still some recent tests point out that other values are available in the literature. For instance, from the test angular size vs. redshift for ultracompact radio sources, it is obtained that Λ has the opposite sign[242].

Moreover, the actual values of ΩΛ have some consistency problem in the standard scenario of inflationary Big Bang. The cosmological constant predicted by the quantum field theory is a value much larger than those derived from observational cosmology.

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether Ω_Λ ≈ 0.7 is robustly established remains under active debate. In 2024–2025 the DESI collaboration reported 2.8–4.2σ evidence that dark energy is evolving rather than constant, and reanalyses of DES-SN5YR with updated SN Ia calibration (Popovic et al., "Dovekie") have shifted significance levels for time-varying dark energy. The huge mismatch with quantum-field-theory vacuum energy (cosmological constant problem) remains unresolved. Thus the inference of a constant Ω_Λ ≈ 0.7 is not uniquely fixed by current data.

status_evidence.title: Dark Energy Survey supernova program: reanalysis with updated SN Ia calibration
status_evidence.snippet: Reanalysis of DES-SN5YR with updated cross-calibration; significance for evolving dark energy revised from 4.2σ to 3.2σ.
status_evidence.claim: SN Ia systematics (calibration) materially affect dark-energy inferences.

status_evidence.title: Dark energy — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: DESI 2024–2025 combined with CMB, weak lensing, and SN data give 2.8–4.2σ evidence for evolving dark energy, with density slowly decreasing in time.
status_evidence.claim: Constant Ω_Λ ≈ 0.7 is being challenged by current data.

status_evidence.title: Cosmological constant — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: QFT estimates of vacuum energy exceed observed Λ by ~120 orders of magnitude; the cosmological constant problem remains unsolved.

status_evidence.title: Super Set of Supernovae Suggests Dark Energy Surprise
status_evidence.snippet: New 2025 supernova compilation suggests dark energy may not be a simple cosmological constant.
status_evidence.claim: Observational support for fixed Ω_Λ ≈ 0.7 is being questioned.
